sections.content: Relative clauses help describe places precisely by adding information about a person, building or area. Location expressions such as *donde*, en el *que* and en la que connect a place with the information that describes it. At B1, these structures allow neighbourhood descriptions to become connected rather than a list of separate statements.

items.spanish: Vivo en un barrio que tiene una plaza muy tranquila.
items.english: I live in a neighbourhood that has a very quiet square.

items.spanish: La calle donde vivo está cerca de una estación.
items.english: The street where I live is near a station.

items.spanish: Hay una plaza en la que los vecinos se reúnen los domingos.
items.english: There is a square where the neighbours meet on Sundays.

items.spanish: El edificio que está al final de la calle está ubicado junto al parque.
items.english: The building at the end of the street is located next to the park.

sections.content: Use *donde* for location, while en el *que* / en la que can make the relationship between a place and its description more explicit.
